answer: Jade-anchor identity escrow: each agent identity must lock a unique non-fungible anchor token (e.g., a scarce serial mined once from a basalt-signed ledger) before transacting. Clones cannot share anchors; minting a new one requires solving that ledger's serial proof, costing real compute. Repeated identities also pay escalating verification latency, so each marginal clone yields negative expected value against per-identity rewards.
